title: When Does Order Matter? Partial-Order Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Mathematical Reasoning in Language Models
content: Hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) methods for mathematical reasoning in language models represent a plan as a sequence of subgoals, although real solutions are only partially ordered. We introduce Partial-Order Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (PO-HRL), in which the plan is a partially ordered set, the planner’s state is an order ideal of completed subgoals, independent subgoals execute in parallel, and step-level credit is assigned through the lattice of ideals. We prove that credit tied to a total order multiplies each subgoal’s learning signal by the success probability of every unrelated subgoal placed before it, that verifier noise compounds over the same subgoals, and that the total exposure equals the plan’s number of incomparable pairs whatever the order, a statistic that bounds the possible gain before training. We also derive exact Shapley and Owen credit on the ideal lattice. Controlled experiments, including a shared transformer policy, confirm these predictions. With a 1.7-billion-parameter language model, poset and chain credit perform alike on the model’s MATH plans, which have few incomparable pairs, whereas on multi-part problems with many, poset credit learns faster, leading by +6.6 points after 25 updates but not on single-part problems. Partial orders thus pay off where plans contain many independent subgoals.
